OIDN-GPU denoiser on ROCm for barney's AMD backends: the cuda backend ships a no-op denoiser which the HIP build reuses; OIDN has a HIP/ROCm device (BARNEY_OIDN_GPU) to wire up as an enhancement. Not required for the correctness gate.

barney hiprt backend: move barney's 12 device programs from the kept megakernel + function-pointer SBT to HIPRT's native 2-D (rayType x geomType) bitcode custom-function-table SBT. Backend 2 ships the megakernel cut (HIPRT does BVH+traversal only, barney's CH/AH/intersect run in-kernel via the SBT pointers); this is the more-native end state, not needed for correctness.

RULING SCOPE (jeffdaily 2026-08-13): prepare the PR branch; a colleague will open the upstream PR on Jeff's behalf.

~65 ports pin CMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx90a before enable_language(HIP), preempting host GPU auto-detect -> non-gfx90a AMD users who omit -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES silently get gfx90a binaries that fail at runtime. Fix = auto-detect + dedup + gfx90a fallback only when no GPU (validated in UCM b697824, carries forward source-class). Audit all ports; PRIORITIZE open PRs; SKIP RAPIDS (ROCm-DS); verify each match is our code not vendored.

Resolved 2026-08-06. Five dependency forks that carried port branches without being tracked are now projects in the organisation: rmagine, opencv, diff-surfel-rasterizations and diff-surfel-tracing, with instant-ngp-kf determined non-contributable and deleted. Each records why its platform row is empty and where its validation actually lives.

Neither utils/check.py nor the pre-push hook notices unresolved conflict markers in a committed file. During the 2026-08-19 fleet sync a merge resolution was committed and pushed to port/colmap with '<<<<<<< HEAD' still in .claude/skills/cuda-to-rocm/references/validation.md, and every gate reported ok; it was caught by hand afterwards and fixed forward in 7deba5c. 'git add' on a conflicted file marks it resolved, so this is easy to do under time pressure and the sweep makes it a bulk operation. A cheap gate would scan tracked text files for '^<<<<<<< ', '^>>>>>>> ' and a '^=======$' between them.

Nothing checks the commit-message rules AGENTS.md states, so a non-compliant body reaches upstream unnoticed. AGENTS.md requires every fork commit to start with [ROCm], keep the title to 72 characters, explain rationale, disclose AI assistance and carry a Test Plan. What exists: jargon.py --port scans the whole branch, but only for in-house vocabulary; pr_intent.py enforces TITLE_MAX=72 on the PULL REQUEST title in CI, not on commit titles; check.py has no commit-message gate; pr_ready checks platform gates and fork cleanliness only. Found on Quest, where c1d7fff shipped with no AI-assistance disclosure and three rounds of gates, review and pr-readiness reporting never mentioned it -- a human reviewer caught it. The same shape as the gh-guard and conflict-marker gates already added: a rule written down but never executed. A cheap gate would walk <fork default>..moat-port for each project with a local clone and check title prefix, title length, and the presence of a disclosure line and a Test Plan in the body.

POLICY (2026-08-24): the C/D-class NVIDIA-notice items (dead-in-tree or text-only: EnvGS orphan script scripts/instant-ngp/colmap_to_nerf.py, OCTproZ about-dialog EULA copy shown even in AMD builds, LichtFeld-Studio nvImageCodec cmake pair, MASt3R-SLAM checkpoints notice, alien/plvs/cupoch vendored CUDA-path helpers, h2o4gpu dead vendored set) are not an immediate issue but should be tidied over time so it is clear AMD is not using them -- BSD swaps or bypass where possible, never deleting licence/notice files. LOW PRIORITY behind the A-class swaps (Velvet, TurboFNO) and pre-fork swaps (h2o4gpu, cuda_voxelizer, PhoenixOS header drop).

The upstream tooling has no path for a SECOND PR on a project whose first PR merged: pr-candidates and upstream.py --review exclude merged projects by design, and pr-ready reports 'pr-exists=the upstream PR is already merged' even when the moat-port branch carries new reviewed+revalidated commits. First hit: TurboFNO 2026-08-24 (three post-merge commits replacing vendor-sample-derived macro text, fully reviewed, platforms carrying forward). Interim: the person opens the follow-up PR manually from the fork and records it with set-pr-open once the tooling permits, or the record is kept in notes. Proper fix: a follow-up-PR flow (review PR on the fork, approval gate, publish) that treats the merged first PR as history rather than a terminal state.
